title: test-0107-MAT-FACTORS
passage: Rohan and Meera were helping their teacher, Mrs. Sharma, organize the school library. They had a box of 12 identical bookmarks to distribute equally among different groups of students. Rohan noted that 1 and 12 are both factors of 12, as every number is divisible by 1 and itself. Meera then pointed out that 2 is the only even prime number, which surprised Rohan. While sorting, they found a stack of 97 cards. Meera checked if it was composite, but realized it had no factors other than 1 and itself, making it a prime number. Next, they looked at the number 15. Rohan said its multiples continue infinitely, not just stopping at 150. Finally, they checked a group of 36 books. Mrs. Sharma explained that prime factorisation must break a number down into prime numbers only, so 36 is 2 × 2 × 3 × 3, not just 4 × 9.
summary: Meera pointed out that 2 is the only even prime number, and it surprised Rohan. Meera checked if it was composite, but realized it had no factors other than 1 and itself, so it was a prime number.
